title.raw: 卷二十七 志第七: 禮儀七 Volume 27 Treatises 7: Rites 7

sentences.zh: 志第七禮儀七

translations.literal: Treatise Seven: Rites Seven.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 7 — Rites 7 (mourning dress).

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，太宗因修禮官奏事之次，言及喪服，太宗曰：「同爨尚有緦麻之恩，而嫂叔無服。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, when Taizong, on an occasion when rites-revising officials were presenting business, spoke of mourning dress, Taizong said: "Those who share a hearth still owe finest-hemp kinship, yet sister-in-law and younger uncle wear none.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 14: while hearing the ritual officers on routine business, Taizong turned to mourning dress. He said that kin who shared a single hearth still owed three months' finest hemp — yet a sister-in-law and her husband's younger brother wore nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 又舅之與姨，親疏相似，而服紀有殊，理未為得。

translations.literal: Again, the mother's brother and the mother's sister are alike in closeness, yet their mourning grades differ — the principle is not yet right.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's brother and a mother's sister were similarly close in feeling, yet the code graded their mourning differently — that could not stand.

sentences.zh: 宜集學者詳議。

translations.literal: It is fitting to gather scholars for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered scholars to deliberate the matter in full.

sentences.zh: 余有親重而服輕者，亦附奏聞。

translations.literal: I also have cases where kinship is heavy yet mourning is light — these too I append for memorial and report." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: He added cases where affection was deep but the prescribed mourning was light, and asked that those be reported as well. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」於是侍中魏徵、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等奏議曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others then submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣聞禮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫，別同異，明是非者也。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that ritual is what resolves doubt, settles hesitation, separates sameness and difference, and clarifies right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual, they wrote, resolves doubt, settles hesitation, separates like from unlike, and shows right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 非從天降，非從地出，人情而已矣。

translations.literal: It does not descend from Heaven, does not emerge from Earth — it is human feeling, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: It does not fall from the sky or rise from the soil; it is nothing but human feeling.

sentences.zh: 夫親族有九，服術有六，隨恩以薄厚，稱情以立文。

translations.literal: Now, kin groups have nine degrees; mourning technique has six grades — following affection for thinness or thickness, fitting feeling to establish pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship has nine degrees; mourning has six grades — affection sets thickness, feeling sets the written rule.

sentences.zh: 然舅之與姨，雖為同氣，論情度義，先後實殊。

translations.literal: Yet the mother's brother and the mother's sister, though of the same breath, when feeling is weighed and principle measured, precedence and posteriority truly differ.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's brother and a mother's sister shared one breath of kin, yet in feeling and principle their precedence was not the same.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 舅為母之本族，姨乃外戚他族，求之母族，姨不在焉，考之經典，舅誠為重。

translations.literal: The mother's brother is the mother's root clan; the mother's sister is external kin, another clan — sought in the mother's clan, the sister is not there; examined in the classics, the brother is truly the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: The mother's brother belonged to her native line; the mother's sister to outside kin. Search the mother's clan and the sister does not appear in it; search the classics and the brother weighs heavier.

sentences.zh: 故周王念齊，每稱舅甥之國；

translations.literal: Thus the Zhou king remembered Qi and often called it the state of maternal uncle and nephew;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou king, remembering Qi, called it the land of uncle and nephew;

sentences.zh: 秦伯懷晉，實切《渭陽》之詩。

translations.literal: the Qin lord yearned for Jin — it truly answers the "Wei-yang" ode.
translations.idiomatic: the Qin lord's longing for Jin answered the Ode's "On the Wei-yang."

sentences.zh: 在舅服止一時，為姨居喪五月，循名喪實，逐末棄本。

translations.literal: for the mother's brother mourning stops at one cycle, yet for the mother's sister one dwells in mourning five months — following the name loses the substance, chasing the branch abandons the root.
translations.idiomatic: mourning for a mother's brother stopped at one year, yet for a mother's sister ran five months — the label had swallowed the substance, the branch had been chased and the root left behind.

sentences.zh: 蓋古人之情，或有未達，所宜損益，實在茲乎！

translations.literal: Perhaps the ancients' feeling in places did not reach clarity — what should be reduced or increased lies here!
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps ancient feeling had not always been clear — here was where the code should be trimmed or enlarged.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也。

translations.literal: The Record says: "A brother's son is like a son.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "A brother's son is as a son —

sentences.zh: 蓋引而進之也；

translations.literal: This is drawing him forward and advancing him;
translations.idiomatic: that is drawing him near and raising him up;

sentences.zh: 嫂叔之不服，蓋推而遠之也。

translations.literal: that sister-in-law and younger uncle do not wear mourning is pushing away and keeping distant." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: that sister-in-law and younger uncle wear none is pushing away and holding at distance." The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」禮：繼父同居，則為之期；

translations.literal: Ritual: for a stepfather with whom one shared a dwelling, one wears mourning for one year;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual fixed one year for a stepfather with whom one had shared a dwelling;

sentences.zh: 未嘗同居，則不為服。

translations.literal: if one never shared a dwelling, one does not wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: if one had never shared a dwelling, no mourning was worn.

sentences.zh: 從母之夫，舅之妻，二夫人相為服。

translations.literal: The mother's sister's husband and the mother's brother's wife — the two ladies wear mourning for each other.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's sister's husband and a mother's brother's wife wore mourning for each other.

sentences.zh: 或曰，同爨緦。

translations.literal: Some say: shared-hearth finest hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Some texts read: finest hemp, as for shared hearth.

sentences.zh: 然則繼父之徒，並非骨肉，服重由乎同爨，恩輕在乎異居。

translations.literal: Thus stepfathers and the like are all not bone-and-flesh — mourning's weight comes from shared hearth, affection's lightness from separate dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Stepfathers and the like were not bone kin — weight came from one hearth, lightness from living apart.

sentences.zh: 故知制服雖繫於名；

translations.literal: Hence one knows that though mourning garments are tied to names,
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garments hung on names,

sentences.zh: 亦緣恩之厚薄者也。

translations.literal: they also follow the thickness or thinness of affection.
translations.idiomatic: yet they also followed how deep affection ran.

sentences.zh: 或有長年之嫂，遇孩童之叔，劬勞鞠養，情若新生，分飢共寒，契闊偕老。

translations.literal: Sometimes there is a sister-in-law of many years who meets a younger uncle still a child — she toils in rearing, feeling like fresh birth, sharing hunger and cold, bound in hardship to grow old together.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes a sister-in-law of long years raises a brother-in-law still a boy — she toils as for a new birth, shares hunger and cold, grows old through hardship beside him.

sentences.zh: 譬同居之繼父，方他人之同爨，情義之深淺，寧可同日而言哉！

translations.literal: It is like a stepfather of shared dwelling compared with another's shared hearth — can the depth of feeling and principle be spoken of on the same day!
translations.idiomatic: That bond is not the same as sharing a hearth with a stranger — how could its depth be weighed on the same scale!

sentences.zh: 在其生也，愛之同於骨肉；

translations.literal: In life one loves him as bone-and-flesh;
translations.idiomatic: In life they loved him as kin;

sentences.zh: 及其死也，則曰推而遠之。

translations.literal: at death one says push away and keep distant.
translations.idiomatic: at death the code said: push away, keep distant.

sentences.zh: 求之本原，深所未諭。

translations.literal: Sought to the root origin — deeply not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Sought to its root, the rule made no sense.

sentences.zh: 若推而遠之為是，則不可生而共居；

translations.literal: If pushing away and keeping distant is right, then in life one cannot dwell together;
translations.idiomatic: If distance were right, they could not have lived together;

sentences.zh: 生而共居之為是，則不可死同行路。

translations.literal: if dwelling together in life is right, then at death one cannot walk the same road.
translations.idiomatic: if living together were right, they could not part on the road at death.

sentences.zh: 重其生而輕其死，厚其始而薄其終，稱情立文，其義安在？

translations.literal: Heavy in life yet light in death, thick at the beginning yet thin at the end — fitting feeling to establish pattern, where is the principle?
translations.idiomatic: Heavy for the living, light for the dead — thick at the start, thin at the end: where was the principle in "fitting feeling to pattern"?

sentences.zh: 且事嫂見稱，載籍非一。

translations.literal: Moreover service to a sister-in-law is praised — the records are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Histories praise devotion to a sister-in-law more than once.

sentences.zh: 鄭仲虞則恩禮甚篤，顏弘都則竭誠致感，馬援則見之必冠，孔伋則哭之為位。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhongyu's ritual affection was very thick; Yan Hongdu's sincerity moved others; Ma Yuan put on his cap whenever he saw her; Kong Ji wept at the appointed place.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhongyu kept ritual affection thick; Yan Hongdu moved others by sincerity; Ma Yuan capped himself whenever he met her; Kong Ji wept in the mourning place.

sentences.zh: 此並躬踐教義，仁深孝友，察其所尚之旨，豈非先覺者歟？

translations.literal: These all personally practiced teaching and righteousness, benevolence deep and filial friendship firm — examining the aim they honored, are they not foreknowers?
translations.idiomatic: Each embodied teaching and righteousness, deep in benevolence and filial bond — judged by what they honored, were they not men who saw ahead?

sentences.zh: 但於其時，上無哲王，禮非下之所議，遂使深情郁乎千載，至理藏於萬古，其來久矣，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: But in their time there was no sage king above, and ritual was not for inferiors to debate — thus deep feeling was pent for a thousand years, ultimate principle hidden for ten thousand generations; the lapse is old — how is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in their day no sage king ruled above, and ritual was not for subjects to debate — deep feeling pent up a thousand years, ultimate principle buried ten thousand generations: a long waste, and a bitter one.

sentences.zh: 今屬欽明在辰，聖人有作，五禮詳洽，一物無遺。

translations.literal: Now we belong to an era when reverent clarity is in the ascendant and the sage acts — the five rites are detailed and complete, not one thing left out.
translations.idiomatic: Now reverent clarity ascends and the sage acts — the five rites are complete, nothing left out.

sentences.zh: 猶且永念慎終，凝神遐想。

translations.literal: Yet he still forever ponders careful completion and gathers his spirit in far thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still ponders careful endings and gathers his mind on what lies far off.

sentences.zh: 以為尊卑之敘，雖煥乎大備；

translations.literal: He holds that the sequence of honored and humble, though brilliant in great completeness,
translations.idiomatic: The order of high and low is brilliantly complete,

sentences.zh: 喪紀之制，或情理未周。

translations.literal: the system of mourning regulations — feeling and principle are not yet everywhere round.
translations.idiomatic: yet mourning regulations still do not everywhere match feeling and principle.

sentences.zh: 爰命秩宗，更詳考正。

translations.literal: Therefore he has charged the Director of Ritual to examine again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He has charged the Director of Ritual to examine them again.

sentences.zh: 臣等奏遵明旨，觸類旁求，採摭群經，討論傳記。

translations.literal: Your subjects, memorializing in accord with the luminous intent, touching categories and seeking widely, gathering the group of classics, debating the transmissions —
translations.idiomatic: Following the imperial intent, we searched widely, gathered classics, debated commentaries —

sentences.zh: 或引兼名實，無文之禮咸秩，惇睦之情畢舉，變薄俗於既往，垂篤義於將來，信六籍所不能談，超百王而獨得者也。

translations.literal: sometimes citing both name and substance, ordering ritual without pattern, raising thick kinship feeling entirely, changing shallow custom of the past, handing down solid righteousness to the future — truly what the six classics cannot discuss, what a hundred kings alone attain.
translations.idiomatic: joining name to substance, ordering what had lacked pattern, raising kinship feeling, changing old shallowness, handing solid righteousness to the future — what the six classics do not say, what only this throne attains alone.

sentences.zh: 諸儒所守，互有異同，詳求厥中，申明聖旨。

translations.literal: What the various Confucians hold differs and agrees — sought carefully for the center, the sage intent is declared.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians differ; we sought the mean and declare the sage intent.

sentences.zh: 謹按曾祖父母舊服齊衰三月，請加為齊衰五月。

translations.literal: We respectfully note: great-great-grandparents formerly wore trimmed sackcloth three months — we request increase to trimmed sackcloth five months.
translations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandparents had worn trimmed sackcloth three months; we ask five months.

sentences.zh: 嫡子婦舊服大功，請加為期。

translations.literal: The principal son's wife formerly wore greater accomplishment — we request increase to one year.
translations.idiomatic: A principal son's wife had worn greater accomplishment; we ask one year.

sentences.zh: 眾子婦小功，今請與兄弟子婦同為大功九月。

translations.literal: The various sons' wives wore lesser accomplishment — we now request the same as brothers' sons' wives: greater accomplishment nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Various sons' wives had worn lesser accomplishment; we ask the same as a brother's son's wife: greater accomplishment, nine months.

sentences.zh: 嫂叔舊無服，今請服小功五月報。

translations.literal: Sister-in-law and younger uncle formerly had no mourning — we now request lesser accomplishment five months in return.
translations.idiomatic: Sister-in-law and younger uncle had worn none; we ask lesser accomplishment five months, with return mourning.

sentences.zh: 其弟妻及夫兄，亦小功五月。

translations.literal: A younger brother's wife and an elder brother of the husband — also lesser accomplishment five months.
translations.idiomatic: A younger brother's wife and a husband's elder brother — also lesser accomplishment five months.

sentences.zh: 舅服緦麻，請與從母同服小功。

translations.literal: The mother's brother wore finest hemp — we request the same as the mother's sister: lesser accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's brother had worn finest hemp; we ask lesser accomplishment, as for a mother's sister.

sentences.zh: 制可之。

translations.literal: The ordinance approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年九月，修禮官長孫無忌等又奏曰：「依古喪服，甥為舅緦麻，舅報甥亦同此制。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Xianqing, rites-revising officials Zhangsun Wuji and others again memorialized, saying: "According to ancient mourning dress, a nephew for his mother's brother wears finest hemp; the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 2, ninth month: Zhangsun Wuji and the ritual revision staff wrote that under the old code a nephew wore finest hemp for his mother's brother, and the uncle reciprocated the same.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年中，八座議奏：『舅服同姨，小功五月。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era the Eight Seats deliberated and memorialized: 'For the mother's brother, mourning is the same as for the mother's sister — lesser accomplishment five months.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan the Eight Seats had ruled that mourning for a mother's brother matched a mother's sister: lesser accomplishment five months.

sentences.zh: 』而今律疏，舅報於甥，服猶三月。

translations.literal: ' Yet in the present Code and Commentaries, the mother's brother's return mourning toward the nephew is still three months.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the current Code and Commentaries still fixed the uncle's return mourning for a nephew at three months.

sentences.zh: 謹按旁尊之服，禮無不報，已非正尊，不敢降也。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that for mourning toward collateral elders, ritual never lacks return mourning; though they are not primary elders, one dare not reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral elders always received return mourning; though not primary kin, the grade must not be cut.

sentences.zh: 故甥為從母五月，從母報甥小功，甥為舅緦麻，舅亦報甥三月，是其義矣。

translations.literal: Thus a nephew for the mother's sister wears five months; the mother's sister's return for the nephew is lesser accomplishment; a nephew for the mother's brother wears finest hemp; the mother's brother also returns finest hemp for the nephew three months — that is the principle.
translations.idiomatic: So a nephew wore five months for a mother's sister, and she returned lesser accomplishment; for a mother's brother he wore finest hemp, and the uncle returned three months' finest hemp — that was the pattern.

sentences.zh: 今甥為舅使同從母之喪，則舅宜進甥以同從母之報。

translations.literal: Now if a nephew for his mother's brother is made the same as mourning for the mother's sister, then the mother's brother ought to advance his return for the nephew to match the mother's sister's return.
translations.idiomatic: If a nephew's mourning for his mother's brother was raised to match a mother's sister, the uncle's return should rise to match her return as well.

sentences.zh: 修律疏人不知禮意，舅報甥服，尚止緦麻，於例不通，禮須改正。

translations.literal: Those who revised the Code and Commentaries did not know ritual intent; the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew still stopping at finest hemp is inconsistent with precedent and ritual must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Code revisers had missed the point: leaving the uncle's return at finest hemp broke precedent and had to be fixed.

sentences.zh: 今請修改律疏，舅報甥亦功。

translations.literal: We now request revision of the Code and Commentaries so that the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew is also lesser accomplishment." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the Code be amended so the uncle's return mourning for a nephew was also lesser accomplishment. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「庶母古禮緦麻，新禮無服。

translations.literal: " They also said: "In ancient ritual a secondary mother was finest hemp; in the new ritual there is no mourning.
translations.idiomatic: They added: ancient ritual required finest hemp for a secondary mother; the new code required none.

sentences.zh: 謹按庶母之子，即是己昆季，為之杖期，而己與之無服。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that sons of a secondary mother are one's own brothers and sisters; for them one wears staff for one year, yet for the secondary mother oneself wears none.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of a secondary mother were full siblings: one wore staff for a year for them, yet wore nothing for the secondary mother herself.

sentences.zh: 同氣之內，吉凶頓殊，求之禮情，深非至理。

translations.literal: Within the same breath, fortune and misfortune suddenly differ — sought in ritual feeling, this is deeply not ultimate reason.
translations.idiomatic: Within one flesh, joy and grief were graded worlds apart — a poor fit to ritual feeling.

sentences.zh: 請依典故，為服緦麻。

translations.literal: We request that according to ancient precedent mourning of finest hemp be worn." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that precedent be restored: finest hemp for a secondary mother. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」制又從之。

translations.literal: " The ordinance again approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved again.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年八月，所司奏：「司文正卿蕭嗣業，嫡繼母改嫁身亡，請申心制。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Longshuo, the relevant office memorialized: "Director of Literary Affairs Xiao Siye's legitimate stepmother remarried and died; he requests to declare heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 2, eighth month: the relevant office reported that Xiao Siye, Director of Literary Affairs, sought heart mourning after his legitimate stepmother remarried and died.

sentences.zh: 據令，繼母改嫁及為長子，並不解官。

translations.literal: According to the ordinance, a stepmother's remarriage and being the eldest son both do not require leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: The code said neither a stepmother's remarriage nor being eldest son required leaving office.

sentences.zh: 」既而有敕：「雖雲嫡母，終是繼母，據禮緣情，須有定制。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict: "Though it is called legitimate mother, in the end it is stepmother — according to ritual, following feeling, there must be a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: though she was called legitimate mother, she was still a stepmother — ritual following feeling required a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 付所司議定奏聞。

translations.literal: Deliver to the relevant office to deliberate, fix, and memorialize." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the relevant offices to deliberate and report. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」司禮太常伯隴西郡王博乂等奏稱：

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Bo Yi, Prince of Longxi Commandery, and others memorialized, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies Bo Yi, Prince of Longxi, and others wrote:

sentences.zh: 緬尋《喪服》，母名斯定，嫡、繼、慈、養，皆在其中。

translations.literal: Tracing the Mourning Dress, the names for mother are thus fixed — legitimate, step, loving, and foster are all within it.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress fixed the names of mother — legitimate, step, loving, and foster all fell within it.

sentences.zh: 惟出母制，特言出妻之子，明非生己，則皆無服。

translations.literal: Only the rule for a mother who has left the household specially speaks of the son of a wife who has left — making clear that if she did not bear one, all wear none.
translations.idiomatic: Only for a mother who had left the household did the text speak of the son of a departed wife — if she had not borne you, you wore none.

sentences.zh: 是以令雲母嫁，又云出妻之子。

translations.literal: Thus the ordinance says when the mother remarries, and again says the son of a wife who has left.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the code spoke of a mother's remarriage and of the son of a departed wife.

sentences.zh: 出言其子，以著所生，嫁即言母，通包養、嫡，俱當解任，併合心喪。

translations.literal: Speaking of the son marks who bore him; speaking of remarriage names the mother — broadly including foster and legitimate, all should leave office, together with heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: "Son" marked who bore you; "remarriage" named the mother — foster and legitimate alike should leave office and observe heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 其不解者，惟有繼母之嫁。

translations.literal: What does not require leaving office is only when the stepmother remarries.
translations.idiomatic: Only a stepmother's remarriage was exempt from leaving office.

sentences.zh: 繼母為名，正據前妻之子；

translations.literal: The name stepmother is properly based on the son of a former wife;
translations.idiomatic: The name stepmother properly applied to the son of a former wife;

sentences.zh: 嫡於諸孽，禮無繼母之文。

translations.literal: among the various sons, legitimate — in ritual there is no text of stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: among various sons by rank, "legitimate stepmother" had no place in ritual text.

sentences.zh: 甲令今既見行，嗣業理申心制。

translations.literal: The first-grade ordinance is now in force; Siye by principle should declare heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The first-grade ordinance was in force; Siye should by rights declare heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 然奉敕議定，方垂永則，令有不安，亦須釐正。

translations.literal: Yet following the edict to deliberate and fix, to hand down an eternal rule — where the ordinance is unsound, it too must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edict sought a lasting rule — where the ordinance was unsound, it too must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 竊以嫡、繼、慈、養，皆非所生，並同行路。

translations.literal: We venture that legitimate, step, loving, and foster — none are those who bore one — all alike do not walk the same road.
translations.idiomatic: Legitimate, step, loving, and foster — none were birth mothers — all alike broke the road of kinship at death.

sentences.zh: 嫁雖比出稍輕，於父終為義絕。

translations.literal: Remarriage, though slightly lighter than leaving the household, toward the father is in the end severance of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Remarriage was slightly lighter than leaving the household, yet toward the father it severed righteousness.

sentences.zh: 繼母之嫁，既殊親母，慈、嫡義絕，豈合心喪？

translations.literal: When the stepmother remarries, she is already unlike the birth mother — loving and legitimate righteousness severed, how can heart mourning fit?
translations.idiomatic: A stepmother's remarriage was unlike a birth mother's; loving and legitimate ties were severed — how could heart mourning fit?

sentences.zh: 望請凡非所生，父卒而嫁，為父後者無服，非承重者杖期，並不心喪，一同繼母。

translations.literal: We hope to request: for all who did not bear one, when the father dies and she remarries — he who becomes father's successor wears none; he who does not bear the weight wears staff for one year — all without heart mourning, the same as stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: We ask: for any non-birth mother who remarried after the father's death — the heir wore none; others wore staff for one year — none with heart mourning, as for a stepmother.

sentences.zh: 有符情禮，無玷舊章。

translations.literal: It accords with feeling and ritual and does not stain the old chapters.
translations.idiomatic: That would match feeling and ritual without staining the old chapters.

sentences.zh: 又心喪之制，惟施服屈，杖期之服，不應解官。

translations.literal: Again, the heart-mourning system applies only when garments are reduced; staff-for-one-year mourning should not require leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Heart mourning applied only when garments were reduced; staff-for-one-year mourning should not require leaving office.

sentences.zh: 而令文三年齊斬，亦入心喪之例；

translations.literal: Yet in the ordinance text three years' trimmed sackcloth also falls under heart mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the code counted three years' trimmed sackcloth as heart mourning;

sentences.zh: 杖期解官，又有妻喪之舛。

translations.literal: staff-for-one-year leaving office also has the error of wife's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: staff-for-one-year leaving office confused wife's mourning as well.

sentences.zh: 又依禮，庶子為其母緦麻三月。

translations.literal: Again, according to ritual, a secondary son for his mother wears finest hemp three months.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual fixed finest hemp three months for a secondary son's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 既是所生母服，准例亦合解官。

translations.literal: Since it is mourning for the mother who bore one, by precedent one should also leave office.
translations.idiomatic: As mourning for the mother who bore him, precedent also required leaving office.

sentences.zh: 令文漏而不言，於事終須修附。

translations.literal: The ordinance text omits and does not speak — in the matter it must finally be revised and appended.
translations.idiomatic: The code omitted that case — it must be revised and appended.

sentences.zh: 既與嫡母等嫁同一令條，總議請改，理為允愜者。

translations.literal: Since it is in the same ordinance article as legitimate mother's remarriage, deliberated together we request change — the principle is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Grouped with legitimate mother's remarriage in one article, we ask a joint revision — the principle is sound.

sentences.zh: 依集文武官九品已上議。

translations.literal: According to gathering civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above were gathered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 得司衛正卿房仁裕等七百三十六人議，請一依司禮狀，嗣業不解官。

translations.literal: From Director of Palace Guards Fang Renyu and seven hundred thirty-six persons — deliberation: request uniform accord with the Director of Ceremonies' position; Siye does not leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Renyu, Director of Palace Guards, and 736 others held with the Director of Ceremonies: Siye need not leave office.

sentences.zh: 得右金吾衛將軍薛孤吳仁等二十六人議，請解嗣業官，不同司禮狀者。

translations.literal: From Right Golden Crow Guard General Xue Guwu Ren and twenty-six persons — deliberation: request removing Siye from office, not agreeing with the Director of Ceremonies' position.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guwu Ren of the Right Golden Crow Guard and 26 others asked that Siye leave office, dissenting from the Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 母非所生，出嫁義絕，仍令解職，有紊緣情。

translations.literal: The mother did not bear one; leaving the household severs righteousness — yet still ordering removal from office disorderly follows feeling.
translations.idiomatic: A non-birth mother's departure severed righteousness — yet still ordering him from office tangled feeling, not clarified it.

sentences.zh: 杖期解官，不甄妻服，三年齊斬，謬曰心喪。

translations.literal: Staff-for-one-year leaving office does not distinguish wife's mourning; three years' trimmed sackcloth is wrongly called heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Staff-for-one-year leaving office failed to distinguish a wife's mourning; three years' trimmed sackcloth was wrongly called heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 庶子為母緦麻，漏其中制。

translations.literal: A secondary son's finest hemp for his mother — the middle regulation is omitted within.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary son's finest hemp for his mother was omitted from the middle grades.

sentences.zh: 此並令文疏舛，理難因襲。

translations.literal: These are all sparse errors in the ordinance text — in principle hard to follow by inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: These were gaps and errors in the code — hard to inherit as they stood.

sentences.zh: 依房仁裕等議，總加修附，垂之不朽。

translations.literal: Following Fang Renyu and the others' deliberation, revise and append in total, to hand down without decay.
translations.idiomatic: Following Fang Renyu's majority, revise and append in full, and hand it down without decay.

sentences.zh: 其禮及律疏有相關涉者，亦請准此改正。

translations.literal: Where ritual and the Code and Commentaries have mutual involvement, we also request correction according to this.
translations.idiomatic: Where ritual and the Code and Commentaries touched the same points, they asked those amended too.

sentences.zh: 嗣業既非嫡母改醮，不合解官。

translations.literal: Siye is not the case of a legitimate mother's remarriage — it is not fitting to remove from office.
translations.idiomatic: Siye's case was not a legitimate mother's remarriage — he should not leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The decree followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。

translations.literal: Heaven honored, Earth humble — Heaven one, Earth two; the positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven stands honored, Earth humble — one and two, yin and yang take their places, and husband and wife are paired.

sentences.zh: 至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。

translations.literal: As for the majesty of death and mourning, the grades of exaltation and reduction — the ritual classic's five-garment system, trimmed and cut garments differ; three years' mourning for father and mother, noble and base without barrier — to repay the kindness of carrying and cherishing, to requite boundless favor.
translations.idiomatic: Death and mourning have their majesty and their grades of rise and fall — five garments in the classic, trimmed sackcloth and cut sackcloth not alike, three years for father and mother without rank — repaying the kindness of the womb, requiting boundless debt.

sentences.zh: 稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。

translations.literal: Examined in high antiquity, mourning periods had no number; reaching the middle age, only then were years fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In deepest antiquity mourning had no fixed term; only in the middle ages did years appear.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；

translations.literal: The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in season — they did not continue one another's music;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in season — music did not pass unchanged;

sentences.zh: 三王異代，不相襲禮。

translations.literal: the Three Kings differed in generation — they did not inherit one another's ritual." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Kings differed in age — ritual did not pass unchanged. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。

translations.literal: The White Tiger Treatise says: "Substance and pattern change twice; correct beginning returns thrice." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The White Tiger Treatise says: "Substance and pattern turn twice; the calendar's start returns threefold." The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。

translations.literal: From after the Duke of Zhou made ritual, since Confucius the father edited the classics — then were distinguished the ceremonies of honored reduction, to mark the nodes of mourning regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After the Duke of Zhou made ritual and Confucius edited the classics, honored reduction was singled out to mark the nodes of mourning law.

sentences.zh: 重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。

translations.literal: Heavy and light follow custom; weigh and pour according to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Weight and lightness followed custom; the code was poured to fit the age.

sentences.zh: 故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。

translations.literal: Hence one knows ritual does not descend from Heaven, does not emerge from Earth — it rests in human messages, only the timely mean.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual does not fall from sky or rise from soil — it lives in human feeling and seeks the mean of the time.

sentences.zh: 春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。

translations.literal: Among the states of Spring and Autumn, Lu knew ritual best — being the Duke of Zhou's descendant, Confucius's homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Among Spring and Autumn states Lu knew ritual best — the Duke of Zhou's line, Confucius's homeland.

sentences.zh: 晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。

translations.literal: Han Qi of Jin came on a mission and said, "Zhou ritual is all in Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi of Jin came visiting and said, "All Zhou ritual is in Lu."

sentences.zh: 」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。

translations.literal: Zhongsun of Qi came to covenant and said, "Lu still holds Zhou ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsun of Qi came to covenant and said, "Lu still holds to Zhou ritual."

sentences.zh: 」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。

translations.literal: Yet there were still Zi-zhang asking about Gaozong's three years in the mourning hut; Zisi not permitting his son to mourn an expelled mother; Zi-you holding that half-brothers of the same mother wear greater accomplishment; Zi-xia holding they should join the trimmed-sackcloth system.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zi-zhang had asked about Gaozong's three years in the mourning hut; Zisi forbade his son mourning an expelled mother; Zi-you set half-brothers of one mother at greater accomplishment; Zi-xia argued for trimmed sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。

translations.literal: These were all of the four categories' number, men of the Ten Wise — high steps in Confucius's gate, personally receiving sage teaching — yet meeting mourning affairs they still doubted thus, which makes clear that from antiquity until now, rise and fall are not one.
translations.idiomatic: They were of the four categories, the Ten Wise — high in Confucius's gate, taught by the sage — yet on mourning they still doubted: from antiquity, rise and fall were never one.

sentences.zh: 三年之制，說者紛然。

translations.literal: On the three-year system, debaters were clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: On the three-year rule, debaters swarmed.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan held it twenty-seven months; Wang Su held twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan counted twenty-seven months; Wang Su twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 又改葬之服，鄭雲服緦三月，王雲訖葬而除。

translations.literal: Again, mourning for reburial — Zheng says wear finest hemp three months; Wang says remove when burial ends.
translations.idiomatic: On reburial: Zheng required finest hemp three months; Wang removed mourning when burial ended.

sentences.zh: 又繼母出嫁，鄭雲皆服，王雲從於繼育，乃為之服。

translations.literal: Again, when the stepmother leaves the household — Zheng says all wear mourning; Wang says only if she reared you is mourning worn.
translations.idiomatic: On a stepmother's remarriage: Zheng required mourning for all; Wang only if she had reared you.

sentences.zh: 又無服之殤，鄭雲子生一月，哭之一日；

translations.literal: Again, the ungarmented infant death — Zheng says if the child lived one month, mourn one day;
translations.idiomatic: On infants who died too young for garments: Zheng set one day of mourning if the child lived one month;

sentences.zh: 王雲以哭之一日易服之月。

translations.literal: Wang says use the month of easy garments for the one day of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang traded the month of garment change for the day of weeping.

sentences.zh: 鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；

translations.literal: Zheng and Wang, ancestors of the classic tradition, each differ and agree; Xun Zhuan gathered antiquity seeking what was lost — each reduced or increased the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Wang, pillars of the tradition, agreed and differed; Xun Zhuan gathered antiquity and trimmed each against the other.

sentences.zh: 荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。

translations.literal: Only then did one know that departing the sage gradually far, fragments and gaps grow more.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the sage only widened the gaps.

sentences.zh: 方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: the house that assembles ritual is named the house of gathered litigation — how could there be fixity!
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: the house that "assembles ritual" is the house of gathered lawsuits — nothing was ever fixed.

sentences.zh: 故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！

translations.literal: Yet "when the father is alive, three years for the mother" has been practiced for more than four reign-periods, coming from the era of the Great Emperor Gaozong, not from the court of Empress Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet "father alive, three years for the mother" had run more than four reigns — born in Gaozong's day, not Wu Zetian's court.

sentences.zh: 而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。

translations.literal: When the Great Emperor ascended the throne, on the day the inner palace submitted the memorial — deliberation of the past could be carried out; entered into the administrative code, worn long already.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne the inner palace had already submitted the memorial; it entered the code and had been worn long.

sentences.zh: 大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。

translations.literal: What a former king approved, sparse and made law;
translations.idiomatic: What a former king approved became sparse commentary and law;

sentences.zh: 前王所是，疏而為律；

translations.literal: what a later king approved, written and made ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: what a later king approved became written ordinance.

sentences.zh: 後王所是，著而為令。

translations.literal: Why must one oppose the former emperor's intent, obstruct the son's feeling, wound pure filial heart, turn the back on virtue and righteousness's root?
translations.idiomatic: Why oppose a former emperor's intent, block a son's feeling, wound pure filial heart, turn from virtue's root?

sentences.zh: 何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？

translations.literal: What harm to sage transformation? What disorder to constant human relations — yet wishing mourning of one cycle, equal to father's younger brother's wife, equal to father's sisters?
translations.idiomatic: What harm to sage rule? What disorder to human relations — yet you would wear one cycle, equal to a father's younger brother's wife, equal to father's sisters?

sentences.zh: 有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？

translations.literal: The three years' mourning is like a white colt crossing a crack — the noble person mourning kin has lifelong sorrow; how much more two cycles!
translations.idiomatic: Three years pass like a white colt through a crack — the noble mourner grieves for life; how much more two full cycles!

sentences.zh: 夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！

translations.literal: Ritual is the body; it is the tread — it shows the footprint.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the body and the tread — it shows the footprint.

sentences.zh: 夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。

translations.literal: Filial piety is cherishing; it is nurturing — by it the heart is sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is cherishing and nurturing — the heart is sustained through it.

sentences.zh: 孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。

translations.literal: Small men are not ashamed of lacking benevolence, do not fear lacking righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Small men are not ashamed to lack benevolence, do not fear to lack righteousness.

sentences.zh: 小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。

translations.literal: Having a system for garments makes fools aspire;
translations.idiomatic: Garments with fixed grades let fools aspire upward;

sentences.zh: 服之有制，使愚人企及；

translations.literal: clothing them in sackcloth makes the sight crush with pain.
translations.idiomatic: dressing them in sackcloth makes the sight crush the heart.

sentences.zh: 衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。

translations.literal: By this to guard people, people still have dying in the morning and forgetting by evening;
translations.idiomatic: With this to guard them, some still die at dawn and forget by dusk;

sentences.zh: 以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；

translations.literal: by this to regulate people, people still have removing garments and following auspicious affairs.
translations.idiomatic: with this to bind them, some still shed garments and chase good fortune.

sentences.zh: 以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。

translations.literal: Now we gradually return to ancient simplicity — filial righteousness must be thickly cultivated; restrain the worthy and draw the foolish — principle relies on quieting in sorrow; eating rice and wearing brocade — what the ear cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The age turns back toward simplicity — filial righteousness must be thickened; restrain the worthy, draw the foolish — principle rests in quieting grief; eating rice and wearing brocade is what the ear cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: If for the various affairs of court audience one followed Zhou ritual entirely, then when men of old saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and grandees presented lambs, geese, jade disks and bi — why not follow now?
translations.idiomatic: If court audience followed Zhou ritual entirely, ancient ministers had presented lambs, geese, disks and bi — why not now?

sentences.zh: 若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？

translations.literal: When Zhou used punishments — tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, amputation — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou punished with tattoo, nose-cutting, castration, amputation — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Zhou had marquis, inner, baron, and guard — court audiences had number — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had marquis, inner, baron, guard — audiences were numbered — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Zhou: not at fifty one does not serve; at seventy one does not enter court — why not follow now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou: not serving before fifty; not entering court at seventy — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？

translations.literal: Zhou had well, hamlet, mound, and outer settlement to establish levies — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou taxed by well, hamlet, mound, and outer settlement — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Zhou had three elders and five ranks — father dies, son succeeds — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had three elders and five ranks — father dies, son succeeds — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Zhou had cap, crown, robe, and fur — chariot riding to battle — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou capped and robed and rode chariots to war — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Zhou divided land and five elders, glue-and-order to nurture the aged — why not practice now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou divided land, kept five elders, schools to nurture the aged — why not now?

sentences.zh: 周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？

translations.literal: Cases like these cannot be exhaustively stated.
translations.idiomatic: Examples like these cannot be counted.

sentences.zh: 諸如此例，不可勝述。

translations.literal: Why alone on the matter of filial thought love one year's mourning for one's mother?
translations.idiomatic: Why alone on filial thought cut a mother's mourning to one year?

sentences.zh: 何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？

translations.literal: What can wound the heart, what can make one wail!
translations.idiomatic: What can wound the heart — what can make one wail!

sentences.zh: 可為痛心，可為慟哭者！

translations.literal: The Ode says: "Alas, alas, parents — bearing me was toil and labor."
translations.idiomatic: The Ode says: "Alas, alas, my parents — to bear me was labor and toil."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。

translations.literal: The Ritual says: "The father's loving the son — he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says: "A father loves his son by loving the worthy and setting aside the incapable;

sentences.zh: 」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；

translations.literal: the mother's loving the son — if worthy then she loves, if incapable then she pities." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: a mother loves her son — if worthy she loves, if incapable she pities. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。

translations.literal: Ruan Jizong was a Jin-era heroic talent, a high man beyond the world — he held the mother heavier than the father.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Jizong was Jin's heroic talent, a man above the world — he held the mother heavier than the father.

sentences.zh: 」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。

translations.literal: Judging by trimmed-sackcloth bolt measure, coarse and fine already reduced — how bear that the node of mourning be reduced to one cycle?
translations.idiomatic: Trimmed sackcloth already graded coarse and fine by bolt — how bear reducing the mourning node to one cycle?

sentences.zh: 據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？

translations.literal: Are men of later ages all ashamed before antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Are later men all ashamed before the ancients?

sentences.zh: 豈後代之士，盡慚於古。

translations.literal: Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following today is not necessarily wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following today not necessarily wrong.

sentences.zh: 循古未必是，依今未必非也。

translations.literal: Again, shared-hearth finest hemp — the ritual classic clarifies the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Again, shared-hearth finest hemp — the classic states the principle clearly.

sentences.zh: 又同爨服緦，禮經明義。

translations.literal: Sister-in-law and younger uncle kept far apart — the same as passers-by on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Sister-in-law and younger uncle were held far apart — as strangers on the road.

sentences.zh: 嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。

translations.literal: Drawing forward and advancing — touching categories and extending.
translations.idiomatic: Draw near and advance — touch a category and extend it.

sentences.zh: 引而進之，觸類而長。

translations.literal: Foster sons all wear hemp and ramie, yet the father's younger brother does not wear finest hemp — pushing distant feeling has surplus, thick kinship righteousness is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Foster sons wore hemp and ramie, yet a father's younger brother wore no finest hemp — distance was overstated, thick kinship understated.

sentences.zh: 猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。

translations.literal: Again, the mother's brothers — feeling cuts to Wei-yang; Zhai Fan sued the injustice done his mother's brother; the Ning clan dwelt in the nephew's phase — my going forth, righteousness is also deep.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's brothers cut feeling to the Wei-yang ode; Zhai Fan sued injustice for his mother's brother; the Ning clan kept the nephew's seat — in my own going forth, the debt is also deep.

sentences.zh: 又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。

translations.literal: Not the same as the mother's sister's honored rank — thus reduced to lesser accomplishment; by the various ancient rituals, popular feeling is offended.
translations.idiomatic: Not the same honored rank as a mother's sister — thus reduced to lesser accomplishment; by ancient ritual, popular feeling was offended.

sentences.zh: 不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。

translations.literal: Now demoting the mother's brother and honoring the mother's sister — this is making today base and antiquity glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Now demoting the mother's brother and honoring the mother's sister — that makes today base and antiquity glorious.

sentences.zh: 今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。

translations.literal: These are all Taizong's regulations — practiced a hundred years already; rashly to cut and restore truly has doubt in use.
translations.idiomatic: These were all Taizong's regulations — practiced a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring was doubtful in practice.

sentences.zh: 此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。

translations.literal: Thereupon debate was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Debate deadlocked.

sentences.zh: 於是紛議不定。

translations.literal: Lübing again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Ritual: when the father is alive, for the mother eleven months then practice; thirteenth month auspicious; fifteenth month end-of-mourning; heart mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: Lübing wrote again, citing the Ritual: while the father lived, for the mother eleven months to practice, thirteenth month auspicious rites, fifteenth month end-of-mourning, and three years' heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 履冰又上疏曰：「《禮》：父在，為母十一月而練，十三月而祥，十五月而禫，心喪三年。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era Empress Wu Zetian submitted a memorial requesting mourning the same as when the father is dead — also not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan Wu had asked for mourning equal to a father's death, but it had not yet taken effect.

sentences.zh: 上元中，則天皇后上表，請同父沒之服，亦未有行。

translations.literal: By the Chuigong era it was first entered into the administrative code; after the change of dynasty the custom then spread in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Chuigong was it written into the code; after the dynastic shift the custom spread.

sentences.zh: 至垂拱年中，始編入格，易代之後，俗乃通行。

translations.literal: Your servant, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, repeatedly requested return to the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, in Kaiyuan 5, repeatedly asked to restore the old rule.

sentences.zh: 臣開元五年，頻請仍舊。

translations.literal: The gracious edict also entrusted mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and mother's brothers and sisters to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also sent mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and maternal kin to the relevant offices for review.

sentences.zh: 恩敕並嫂叔舅姨之服，亦付所司詳議。

translations.literal: The offices' deliberations mixed agreement and difference.
translations.idiomatic: The offices split.

sentences.zh: 諸司所議，同異相參。

translations.literal: The relevant office alone held to the text on trimmed and cut garments, and also said it accorded with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: One office clung to the trimmed-sackcloth articles and called that canonical.

sentences.zh: 所司惟執齊斬之文，又曰亦合典禮。

translations.literal: I observe that the newly revised code still follows the Chuigong error, so that when grandparents are alive and a grandson's wife dies, in the lower apartments a second full cycle is also observed — most meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: The new code still followed Chuigong's error: with grandparents alive and a grandson's wife dead, lower apartments sometimes observed a second full cycle — absurd.

sentences.zh: 竊見新修之格，猶依垂拱之偽，致有祖父母安存，子孫之妻亡沒，下房筵幾，亦立再周，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: According to the Changes, Family hexagram: "It profits the woman's constancy; the woman holds correct position within, the man holds correct position without.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes, Family hexagram, says: constancy profits the woman; she holds correct position within, the man without.

sentences.zh: 據《周易·家人》卦云：『利女貞女正位於內，男正位於外。

translations.literal: Man and woman correct — this is the great principle of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Correct man and woman embody Heaven and Earth's great principle.

sentences.zh: 男女正，天地之大義。

translations.literal: The family has a stern lord — this means father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: A household has a stern lord: father and mother.

sentences.zh: 家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。

translations.literal: Father as father, son as son, elder brother as elder brother, younger brother as younger brother, husband as husband, wife as wife — the family way is correct and the realm is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Father father, son son, elder brother elder brother, younger brother younger brother, husband husband, wife wife — right the family and the realm follows.

sentences.zh: 父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、婦婦，家道正而天下正矣。

translations.literal: The Ritual: "A woman in the chamber takes the father as Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says: in the chamber a woman takes her father as Heaven;

sentences.zh: 』《禮》：『女在室，以父為天；

translations.literal: after marriage, she takes the husband as Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: after marriage she takes her husband as Heaven."

sentences.zh: 出嫁，以夫為天。

translations.literal: Again: "At home she follows the father; after marriage she follows the husband; when the husband dies she follows the son."
translations.idiomatic: Again: at home she follows the father, in marriage the husband, in widowhood the son."

sentences.zh: 』又：『在家從父，出嫁從夫，夫死從子。

translations.literal: Fundamentally there is no law of self-willed defiance of elders.
translations.idiomatic: There is no charter for defying elders on one's own.

sentences.zh: 』本無自專抗尊之法。

translations.literal: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, the state no two lords, the family no two elders — one principle governs.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, a state no two lords, a family no two elders — one principle rules all.

sentences.zh: 即《喪服四制》云：『天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother is one cycle — to avoid two elders." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Hence while the father lives, mourning for the mother is one cycle — to avoid two elders in one house. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 故父在為母服周者，避二尊也。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty rightly holds family and state and filially governs the realm, yet does not decide in the imperial heart and correct this ritual in detail — do not follow vulgar custom and indulge children's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rightly orders family and state by filial rule, yet has not settled this rite in the imperial heart — do not follow custom and indulge a child's feeling alone.

sentences.zh: 』伏惟陛下正持家國，孝理天下，而不斷在宸衷，詳正此禮，無隨末俗，顧念兒女之情。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that later ages will again have women who usurp their husbands' government." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fears later ages will again see wives seize their husbands' authority. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 臣恐後代復有婦奪夫政之敗者。」

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not answered.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 疏奏未報。

translations.literal: Lübing again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Lübing wrote again.

sentences.zh: 履冰又上奏曰：

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the way of husband and wife is the beginning of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The way of husband and wife, he wrote, is where human relations begin.

sentences.zh: 臣聞夫婦之道，人倫之始。

translations.literal: Honored and humble take law from Heaven and Earth; movement and rest accord with yin and yang — yin and yang harmonize and Heaven and Earth generate; husband and wife are correct and human relations take their pattern.
translations.idiomatic: High and low take law from Heaven and Earth; movement and rest match yin and yang — yin and yang harmonize and the world is born; husband and wife are right and human relations fall into order.

sentences.zh: 尊卑法於天地，動靜合於陰陽，陰陽和而天地生成，夫婦正而人倫式序。

translations.literal: From regulating the family to punishing the state — the hen does not crow at dawn; the four virtues' ritual is not transgressed; the three followings' principle stands there.
translations.idiomatic: From family discipline to state punishment — the hen does not crow at dawn; the four virtues are not breached; the three followings stand firm.

sentences.zh: 自家刑國，牝雞無晨，四德之禮不愆，三從之義斯在。

translations.literal: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, the state no two lords, the family no two elders — one principle governs.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, a state no two lords, a family no two elders — one principle rules all.

sentences.zh: 即《喪服四制》云：「天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother is one cycle — to show there are not two elders." The passage concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Hence while the father lives, mourning for the mother is one cycle — to show there are not two elders in one house. The passage concluded."

sentences.zh: 故父在為母服周者，見無二尊也。

translations.literal: According to old observance, when the father is alive mourning for the mother is one cycle until removal of the spirit tablet, two cycles heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Old observance fixed one cycle until tablet removal for a mother while the father lived, and two cycles of heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 」准舊儀，父在為母一週除靈，再周心喪。

translations.literal: That the father must wait three years before marrying again — this penetrates the son's intent.
translations.idiomatic: That a father waited three years before remarrying penetrated the son's intent.

sentences.zh: 父必三年而後娶者，達子之志焉。

translations.literal: How could the former sage be without feeling toward those who bore him — he firmly had intent toward family and state.
translations.idiomatic: The former sage was not without feeling for those who bore him — he firmly held family and state in view.

sentences.zh: 豈先聖無情於所生，固有意於家國者矣。

translations.literal: Tracing it: in the inaugural year of Shangyuan, Zetian already secretly held government, about to plot usurpation, beforehand exalting her kin.
translations.idiomatic: Trace it to Shangyuan's first year: Wu already held power in secret, plotting usurpation, exalting her kin beforehand.

sentences.zh: 原夫上元肇年，則天已潛秉政，將圖僭篡，預自崇先。

translations.literal: Tracing it to the root: in the inaugural year of Shangyuan, Zetian already secretly held government, about to plot usurpation, beforehand exalting her kin.
translations.idiomatic: At the root: Shangyuan's first year found Wu already ruling in secret, plotting usurpation, exalting her line beforehand.

sentences.zh: 請升慈愛之喪，以抗尊嚴之禮，雖齊斬之儀不改，而几筵之制遂同。

translations.literal: We ask to raise mourning for loving-kindness to resist the ritual of honored dignity; though the qi and zhan ceremonies are unchanged, the regulations for mats and tables are thereby made the same.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to elevate affectionate mourning to counter dignified ritual: though qi and zhan forms stay unchanged, the mat-and-table rules would become the same.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，尚未通用。

translations.literal: Within several years it had still not been put into general use.
translations.idiomatic: For several years it still was not generally adopted.

sentences.zh: 天皇晏駕，中宗蒙塵。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Emperor passed away; Zhongzong suffered dust on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died; Zhongzong was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 垂拱之末，果行聖母之偽符；

translations.literal: At the end of the Chuigong era, the Holy Mother's false tally was indeed put into practice;
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chuigong, the Empress Dowager's false mandate was carried out;

sentences.zh: 載初之元，遂啟易代之深釁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zai Chu, the deep breach of changing the dynasty was thereupon opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zai Chu the deep wound of dynastic usurpation was opened.

sentences.zh: 孝和雖名反正，韋氏復效晨鳴。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Xiaohe was nominally restored to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the cock's dawn crow.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaohe was nominally restored, the Wei clan again played the cock that crows at dawn.

sentences.zh: 孝和非意暴崩，韋氏旋即稱制。

translations.literal: Xiaohe died unexpectedly not by intent; the Wei clan at once assumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohe died suddenly and without design; the Wei clan immediately seized power.

sentences.zh: 不蒙陛下英算，宗廟何由克復？

translations.literal: Had we not received Your Majesty's brilliant calculation, how could the ancestral temple have been recovered?
translations.idiomatic: Without Your Majesty's brilliant resolve, how could the ancestral temple have been restored?

sentences.zh: 《易》云：「臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "A minister kills his lord, a son kills his father—not the work of a single morning or evening."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "When a minister kills his lord or a son his father, it is not the work of a single morning or evening."

sentences.zh: 」其斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: " This is what it speaks of.
translations.idiomatic: That is precisely what it means.

sentences.zh: 臣謹尋禮意，防杜實深，若不早圖刊正，何以垂戒於後？

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully traces ritual intent: prevention and blocking are truly deep; if we do not early plan to correct the text, how may we hand down a warning to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has traced the ritual logic: the safeguards are profound; unless the text is corrected soon, what warning can posterity receive?

sentences.zh: 所以薄言禮教，請依舊章，恩敕通明，蒙付所司詳議。

translations.literal: Therefore we speak briefly of ritual teaching, ask to follow the old statutes, that the gracious edict be made clear, and be entrusted to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hence we speak briefly of ritual teaching and ask to follow the old statutes; may the gracious edict be made clear and the matter sent to the responsible offices for full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 且臣所獻者，蓋請正夫婦之綱，豈忘母子之道。

translations.literal: Moreover what your servant presents is fundamentally a request to rectify the bond of husband and wife—how could we forget the way of mother and son?
translations.idiomatic: What your servant offers chiefly seeks to rectify the bond of husband and wife; we do not forget the way of mother and son.

sentences.zh: 諸議多不討其本源，所非議者，大凡只論罔極之恩；

translations.literal: Most deliberators do not examine the root source; what they oppose is, in the main, only the argument of boundless favor;
translations.idiomatic: Most debaters do not reach the root; their objections chiefly invoke boundless parental favor alone;

sentences.zh: 喪也寧戚；

translations.literal: "In mourning, better ke than wei";
translations.idiomatic: "In mourning, better distress than ease";

sentences.zh: 禽獸識母而不識父；

translations.literal: "Beasts know the mother and do not know the father";
translations.idiomatic: "Beasts know their mother but not their father";

sentences.zh: 秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑；

translations.literal: "After Qin burned the books the ritual classics were incomplete; later Confucians compiled and gathered them—insufficient to be relied on";
translations.idiomatic: "After Qin burned the books the ritual classics were broken; later Confucians pieced them together and they cannot be fully trusted";

sentences.zh: 豈得與伯叔母服同，豈得與姑姊妹制等；

translations.literal: "How can it be the same as mourning for an uncle's wife, how can it equal the regulation for paternal aunts and sisters";
translations.idiomatic: "How can it match an uncle's wife's mourning, or equal the rule for paternal aunts and sisters";

sentences.zh: 三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂；

translations.literal: "The three kings do not inherit one another's ritual; the five emperors do not continue one another's music";
translations.idiomatic: "The three kings do not pass down one another's ritual; the five emperors do not continue one another's music";

sentences.zh: 齊斬足為升降，歲年何忍不同：此並道聽途說之言，未習先王之旨，又安足以議經邦理俗之禮乎？

translations.literal: "Qi and zhan suffice for rise and fall—how can the years bear to differ: these are all words heard on the road and passed along, men who have not studied the former kings' intent—how are they fit to deliberate ritual for ordering the state and governing custom?"
translations.idiomatic: "Qi and zhan are enough for gradation—how can the years be made different? These are roadside rumors from men untrained in the former kings; how can they debate statecraft and custom?"

sentences.zh: 臣請據經義以明之。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to clarify by the classics' meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant will clarify this by the classics.

sentences.zh: 所云「罔極之恩」者，春秋祭祀，以時思之。

translations.literal: What is called "boundless favor" is spring and autumn sacrifice—thinking of them at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: "Boundless favor" means seasonal sacrifice in spring and autumn—remembering parents at the proper times.

sentences.zh: 君子有終身之憂，霜露之感，豈止一二周之服哉！

translations.literal: The gentleman has lifelong sorrow; feeling at frost and dew—is it only one or two cycles of mourning dress?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman mourns for life; frost and dew move him—this is not exhausted in one or two cycles of dress alone.

sentences.zh: 故聖人恐有朝死而夕忘，曾鳥獸之不若，為立中制，使賢不肖共成文理而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage feared that one might die in the morning and forget by evening, not even equal to birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation so worthy and unworthy alike might together complete pattern and principle.
translations.idiomatic: The sage feared morning death and evening forgetting—worse than beasts—and set a middle rule so all alike could keep pattern and principle.

sentences.zh: 所云「喪也寧戚」者，孔子答林放之問。

translations.literal: What is called "in mourning, better ke than wei" is Confucius' answer to Lin Fang's question.
translations.idiomatic: "In mourning, better ke than wei" is Confucius answering Lin Fang.

sentences.zh: 至如太奢太儉，太易太戚，皆非禮中。

translations.literal: As for too lavish or too frugal, too easy or too ke—none is within ritual's mean.
translations.idiomatic: Too lavish or too frugal, too easy or too ke—none hits ritual's mean.

sentences.zh: 苟不得中，名為俱失，不如太儉太戚焉。

translations.literal: If one cannot hit the mean, both are called lost; better too frugal and too ke.
translations.idiomatic: Missing the mean, both fail; still better too frugal and too ke.

sentences.zh: 毀而滅性，猶愈於朝死夕忘焉。

translations.literal: Destroying the person and extinguishing nature is still better than dying in the morning and forgetting by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Ruining oneself in grief is still better than forgetting by evening what died in the morning.

sentences.zh: 此論臨喪哀毀之容，豈比於同宗異姓之服？

translations.literal: This discusses the countenance of mourning grief at the coffin—how can it be compared with mourning dress for kin of the same clan and different surnames?
translations.idiomatic: That concerns grief at the bier—not mourning grades for agnates and affines.

sentences.zh: 所云「禽獸識母而不識父」者，禽獸群居而聚筜，而無家國之禮，少雖知親愛其母，長不解尊嚴其父。

translations.literal: What is called "beasts know the mother and do not know the father": beasts herd together in nests and have no ritual of family and state; young though they know to love the mother, grown they do not understand to honor the father.
translations.idiomatic: "Beasts know mother not father": they nest in herds without family or state ritual; young love the mother, but grown they do not honor the father.

sentences.zh: 引此為諭則亦禽獸之不若乎！

translations.literal: To cite this as a parallel—is one then not even the equal of beasts!
translations.idiomatic: To argue from that is to fall below beasts!

sentences.zh: 所云「秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑」者，人間或有遺逸，豈亦家戶到而燔之」假若盡燔，苟不可信，則墳黃都謬，庠序徒立，非聖之談，復雲安屬？

translations.literal: What is called "after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were incomplete; later Confucians compiled—insufficient to rely on": among men there may be omissions and losses—did every household reach and burn them? If all were burned and nothing can be trusted, then the Yellow Mound and the schools would all be wrong, the halls of learning would stand in vain—of what would non-sage talk again belong?
translations.idiomatic: "After Qin burned the books the classics were broken and later Confucians pieced them together": some texts were lost, but not every house was burned. If none may be trusted, then the Yellow Mound and the schools are all wrong and non-sage talk has no place left.

sentences.zh: 所云「與伯叔姑姊服同」者，伯叔姑姊有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？

translations.literal: What is called "the same mourning as for paternal uncles and aunts and sisters": do paternal uncles and aunts and sisters have the mat-and-staff regulation and three years' heart mourning?
translations.idiomatic: "Same as uncles and aunts and sisters": do they wear mat and staff with three years' heart mourning?

sentences.zh: 所云「五帝不相沿樂，不相襲禮」，誠哉是言！

translations.literal: What is called "the five emperors do not continue music, do not inherit ritual"—truly those words!
translations.idiomatic: "The five emperors do not continue music or inherit ritual"—how true!

sentences.zh: 此是則天懷私苞禍之情，豈可復相沿樂襲禮乎？

translations.literal: This is the feeling of Zetian harboring private intent and wrapping calamity—how can one again continue music and inherit ritual?
translations.idiomatic: That was Zetian's private scheming—how can music and ritual be continued on that basis?

sentences.zh: 所云「齊斬足為升降」者，母齊父斬，不易之禮。

translations.literal: What is called "qi and zhan suffice for rise and fall": mother in qi, father in zhan—unchanging ritual.
translations.idiomatic: "Qi and zhan suffice for gradation": mother in qi, father in zhan—unchanging ritual.

sentences.zh: 按《三年問》云：「將由修飾之君子與，三年之喪，若駟之過隙，遂之，則是無窮也。

translations.literal: According to the Three Years Question: "Is it with the gentleman who cultivates ornament? Three years' mourning is like a team of horses passing a crack; to follow it is endless."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Years Question asks: "For the ornamented gentleman, three years' mourning is like horses through a crack; to follow it endlessly is impossible."

sentences.zh: 然則何以周也？

translations.literal: Then why fix it at a cycle?
translations.idiomatic: Why then fix it at one cycle?

sentences.zh: 曰：至親以周斷。

translations.literal: It says: The closest kin are cut off at a cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: the closest kin are cut off at one cycle.

sentences.zh: 是何也？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 曰：天地則已易矣，四時則已變矣，其在天地之者，莫不更始焉，以是象之也。

translations.literal: It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already shifted; what is between Heaven and earth—none does not begin anew; thereby it is imaged.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth have changed, the four seasons shifted; all between them begin anew—this is the image.

sentences.zh: 然則何以三年？

translations.literal: Then why three years?
translations.idiomatic: Why then three years?

sentences.zh: 曰：加重焉耳。

translations.literal: It says: Only to add weight.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: only to add weight.

sentences.zh: 」故父加至再周，父在為母加三年心喪。

translations.literal: " Therefore for the father it is increased to two cycles; when the father is alive, for the mother it adds three years' heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the father reaches two cycles; while the father lives, for the mother three years' heart mourning are added.

sentences.zh: 今者還同父沒之制，則尊厭之律安施？

translations.literal: Now to return to the same regulation as when the father has died—where is the law of honored reduction applied?
translations.idiomatic: Now to match the rule when the father is dead—where does honored reduction apply?

sentences.zh: 《喪服四制》又曰：「凡禮之大體，體天地，法四時，則陰陽，順人情，故謂之禮。

translations.literal: The Mourning Dress Four Principles also says: "The great body of all ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, patternizes yin and yang, follows human feeling—therefore it is called ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress Four Principles: "Ritual's great body embodies Heaven and earth, follows the four seasons, patterns yin and yang, and accords with human feeling."

sentences.zh: 」訾之者是不知禮之所由生。

translations.literal: " Those who criticize it do not know where ritual comes from.
translations.idiomatic: Critics do not know where ritual comes from.

sentences.zh: 非徒不識禮之所由制，亦恐未達孝子之通義。

translations.literal: They not only fail to know where ritual is fashioned; they also probably have not grasped the filial son's comprehensive meaning.
translations.idiomatic: They not only miss how ritual is made; they likely miss the filial son's full meaning.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《孝經》，以明陛下孝治之合至德要道，請論世欲訾禮之徒。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully cites the Classic of Filial Piety to show that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and asks to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cites the Classic of Filial Piety to show Your Majesty's filial rule fits utmost virtue and the essential way, and answers those who would criticize ritual.

sentences.zh: 夫至德謂孝悌，要道謂禮樂。

translations.literal: Utmost virtue is called filial piety and brotherliness; the essential way is called ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost virtue is filial piety and brotherliness; the essential way is ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 「移風易俗，莫善於樂，安上治民，莫善於禮。

translations.literal: "To shift custom and change the vulgar, nothing is better than music; to settle those above and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual."
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing shifts custom like music; nothing settles superiors and governs people like ritual."

sentences.zh: 」又《禮》有「無體之禮，無聲之樂。

translations.literal: " Again the Ritual has "ritual without bodily form, music without sound."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual also speaks of "formless ritual" and "soundless music."

sentences.zh: 」按《孝經援神契》云：「天子孝曰就，就之為言成也。

translations.literal: " According to the Filial Piety Apocryphal God's Covenant: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called jiu; jiu means completion."
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Piety Apocryphal God's Covenant: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called jiu—completion."

sentences.zh: 天子德被天下，澤及萬物，始終成就，則其親獲安，故曰就也。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers all under Heaven and his grace reaches the ten thousand things, beginning and end are accomplished, then his parents obtain peace—therefore it is called jiu.
translations.idiomatic: When his virtue covers the realm and grace reaches all things, beginning and end complete, his parents are secure—hence jiu.

sentences.zh: 諸侯孝曰度，度者法也。

translations.literal: The feudal lord's filial piety is called du; du means law.
translations.idiomatic: A feudal lord's filial piety is called du—law.

sentences.zh: 諸侯居國，能奉天子法度，得不危溢，則其親獲安，故曰度也。

translations.literal: When the feudal lord dwells in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not reaching danger and excess, then his parents obtain peace—therefore du.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in his state, if he upholds the Son of Heaven's laws without danger or excess, his parents are secure—hence du.

sentences.zh: 卿大夫孝曰譽，譽之為言名也。

translations.literal: The grandee and great officer's filial piety is called yu; yu means name.
translations.idiomatic: A grandee's filial piety is called yu—reputation.

sentences.zh: 卿大夫言行佈滿，能無惡稱，譽達遐邇，則其親獲安，故曰譽也。

translations.literal: When the grandee's words and conduct spread everywhere and he can be without evil reputation, fame reaching far and near, then his parents obtain peace—therefore yu.
translations.idiomatic: If his words and conduct spread without evil fame, near and far, his parents are secure—hence yu.

sentences.zh: 士孝曰究，究者以明審為義。

translations.literal: The shi's filial piety is called jiu; jiu means clarity and scrutiny in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: A shi's filial piety is called jiu—scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 士始升朝，辭親入仕，能審資父事君之禮，則其親獲安，故曰究也。

translations.literal: When the shi first ascends court, leaves parents and enters service, and can scrutinize the ritual of supporting the father and serving the lord, then his parents obtain peace—therefore jiu.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering court he scrutinizes how to support father and serve lord—then his parents are secure; hence jiu.

sentences.zh: 庶人孝曰畜，畜者含畜為義。

translations.literal: The commoner's filial piety is called xu; xu means containing and storing in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner's filial piety is called xu—containment.

sentences.zh: 庶人含情受朴，躬耕力作，以畜其德，則其親獲安，故曰畜也。

translations.literal: The commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plows and labors with strength, thereby storing his virtue—then his parents obtain peace—therefore xu.
translations.idiomatic: He contains feeling, accepts simplicity, plows and labors, stores virtue—then his parents are secure; hence xu.

sentences.zh: 」陛下以韋氏構逆，中宗降禍，宸衷哀憤，睿情卓烈。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty, because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered calamity, the imperial heart was sorrowful and indignant, sagely feeling outstanding and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, when the Wei clan rebelled and Zhongzong suffered calamity, bore sorrow and indignation in the imperial breast with outstanding sagely resolve.

sentences.zh: 初無一旅之眾，遂殄九重之妖，定社稷於阽危，拯宗枝於塗炭。

translations.literal: At first without a single company of men, you thereupon extinguished the demons of the ninefold palace, settled the altars of soil and grain on the brink of peril, and rescued the lineage branches from charcoal.
